text: three functions accept center scale arguments, applied IRLS-weighted design matrix computing diagnostic (ignored whenever method supplied). accept values base R’s scale(): center: FALSE (default), TRUE (subtract column’s mean), numeric vector per-column values subtract. scale: "unit" (default; Euclidean/L2 unit-length columns, originally proposed transformation), TRUE (root-mean-square scaling), FALSE (scaling), numeric vector per-column divisors. scale = TRUE rescales every eigenvalue factor (nrow(X) - 1) relative default scale = "unit", CN sqrt(CN) unaffected; scale = FALSE custom numeric vector generally change , since columns longer put comparable scale. use center = TRUE intercept model unless know : canonical-link GLM, IRLS-weighted design matrix satisfies Xw %*% coef(mod) == 1 exactly, centering intercept column guaranteed drop matrix’s rank exactly one. precisely Belsley, Kuh Welsch (1980) recommend centering collinearity diagnostics; bkw_diagnostics() rvif_diagnostics() detect raise informative error instead returning NaN.
code: condition_number(mod, scale = TRUE) # root-mean-square scaling instead of unit length #> Eigenvalues of X_unit'X_unit (decreasing order): #> [1] 649.9211 175.4071 123.5469  46.0607   0.0642 #>  #> CN (eigenvalue scale): 10123.1410 #> sqrt(CN) (classical, singular-value scale): 100.6138 bkw_diagnostics(mod, center = TRUE) #> Error: #> ! The (weighted, transformed) design matrix is exactly rank-deficient, so the variance-decomposition proportions are undefined. Two known causes: (1) centering (center = TRUE) an IRLS-weighted design matrix that includes an intercept, for some family/link combinations (this is not a general canonical-link fact -- e.g. binomial with the logit link is unaffected); and (2) the Gamma family with its canonical (inverse) link, for which sqrt(w) * linear.predictors is exactly 1 for every observation regardless of whether an intercept is present, so removing the intercept does not avoid it there. This is exactly why Belsley, Kuh and Welsch recommend against centering for collinearity diagnostics; use the default center = FALSE, or remove the exact collinearity from the data.
